prompt.context: Your client is National Logistics; a large transportation and logistics company that delivers freight to all areas of North America. Over the last five years, the company has experienced rising costs due to increases in wages resulting from a shortage of truckers. The client is now looking to reduce operational costs in the business.
prompt.question: How would you advise the client?

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's primary goal?
clarifying_info.a: National Logistics is looking to boost profitability by any means.

clarifying_info.q: Are other competitors facing the same issue?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the entire transportation industry is feeling the wage pressure.

clarifying_info.q: Does the client have a profitability target?
clarifying_info.a: No, the client just wants to improve profitability from their current state.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other costs that have been influencing profitability?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, steadily rising fuel prices have also been hampering the company's profits.

clarifying_info.q: Is the company running at full capacity?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the only thing limiting revenue growth is finding drivers to drive their trucks.

clarifying_info.q: Has revenue also been in decline?
clarifying_info.a: No, revenue has been rising steadily over the last 5 years but is only capped by lack of drivers to fulfill deliveries.

exhibits.title: Cost of Operating Each Semi
exhibits.shows: A table comparing financial metrics for a Standard Truck versus a Hybrid Truck across purchase price, maintenance per year, insurance per year, average miles driven per year, MPG, and vehicle lifespan. A footnote states the company pays an average $3.00 per gallon for fuel.

framework: Profitability lens: split into Revenue drivers and Cost drivers
Revenue levers: pricing power, delivery/freight mix, double-trailers per run
Cost levers: fuel (hedging, efficiency), depreciation (truck lifespan), overhead/admin, outsourcing/contract labor, load optimization per truck
Investment options: buy fuel-efficient/hybrid trucks, add energy-saving technology (spoilers, speed limiters, drag-resistant wheels), acquire a low-cost transportation firm
Innovation options: autonomous trucks, drone delivery for short routes
Diversification: explore higher-margin adjacent markets such as air freight, shipping, or railways

questions.prompt: The client is interested in purchasing more fuel-efficient hybrid truck fleets that use both batteries and diesel fuel. What are some of the cost considerations the client should be aware of in making this decision?
questions.guidance: Candidate must identify all five key cost factors: (1) Purchase price/cost of truck, (2) Maintenance, (3) Insurance, (4) Miles per gallon (fuel usage), (5) Depreciation. Bonus: which costs would increase with hybrid trucks? Strong answer: purchase price, maintenance, and insurance all increase because hybrid models have more technology and greater complexity.

questions.prompt: We ran two cost scenarios for the client to compare the cost of operating a hybrid truck vs. a standard diesel truck. What are the potential cost savings (if any) from switching to a hybrid truck?
questions.guidance: Candidate should ask about the depreciation schedule. Answer: straight-line depreciation, $0 salvage value at end of lifespan. Candidate must compute total annual cost for each truck type and compare. The result is that annual costs are identical — there are no net savings.

math.setup: Annual cost = Maintenance + Insurance + Depreciation + Fuel. Depreciation = Purchase Price / Lifespan. Fuel cost = (Miles/Year / MPG) x Price per gallon.
math.answer: There are no annual cost savings; both truck types cost $35,000 per truck per year to operate.

questions.prompt: Given the results of the analysis, would you recommend National Logistics invest in hybrid trucks? Why or why not?
questions.guidance: No single right answer — question tests business judgment under ambiguity. YES rationales: savings increase if fuel prices rise; lifespan extension reduces depreciation; room to negotiate maintenance/insurance; environmental benefits and potential tax advantages. NO rationales: fuel prices may fall making standard trucks cheaper; hybrid investment does not directly address the primary goal of reducing costs given zero current savings; capital tied up in new trucks creates opportunity cost versus other initiatives. Interviewer judges whether rationale is sound.

brainstorming.prompt: The client also wants to get our thoughts on how they can reduce their shortage of truckers. Brainstorm some ways National Logistics can reduce their shortage.

categories.name: Internal – Pay and Benefits (note: these reduce profitability)
Internal – Leverage Existing Staff
ideas: Have overhead/admin employees drive during peak seasons

categories.name: External
ideas: Hire contract drivers part-time during peak seasons
Sponsor international drivers with work visas
Explore heavy-duty drones for short routes

recommendation: State a clear yes or no on investing in hybrid trucks with supporting rationale
If not investing, identify other cost-saving initiatives from the framework (fuel hedging, load optimization, outsourcing, overhead reduction)
risks: Fuel price movements will directly impact cost savings or losses from the hybrid investment
Maintenance costs may vary and exceed estimates, eroding the hybrid's breakeven position
Driver wages may continue to rise in a strong economy, further pressuring profitability
next_steps: Explore other cost-savings alternatives identified in the framework (double trailers, load optimization, admin reduction)
Investigate ways to reduce hybrid truck insurance premiums or negotiate maintenance contracts
Model sensitivity of the hybrid investment under different fuel price scenarios
